scene.title: A place at the table

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: From an earlier evening in the house, a conversation worth keeping.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: I've got two cups and one important question. Tea, or the terrible cocoa I keep trying to improve?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One cup has a chip in the handle. The other has a crooked flower painted on it.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: That flower was meant to be a fox. You can be kind about it, but please don't lie.

scene.memory: A cup was kept for you here, before the house asked you for anything.

response.speaker: fox
response.text: Brave. I mean about the cocoa. The flower is excellent company.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She moves the chipped cup to her own place.

response.speaker: fox
response.text: It suits your hand, doesn't it? I keep forgetting that a thing can be chipped and still be exactly right.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She puts the cocoa away and does not look disappointed.

scene.title: A little worried face

lines.speaker: axolotl
lines.text: This is PLUM! He's on his morning lap of the tank, worried face and all. He usually stops swimming when I laugh.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Axel blows a crooked bubble. PLUM noses it, then turns back to him.

lines.speaker: axolotl
lines.text: He's old for a fish. I keep forgetting how quickly somebody else can get old.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His small hand follows PLUM along the glass, close but never touching.

scene.memory: PLUM stops swimming when Axel laughs. It is a small thing, and it matters.

scene.title: The same word

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Below the house, the word you offered catches against the rim instead of sinking.

lines.speaker: owl
lines.text: Wait. I wrote that word in my notebook this morning. Before you brought it down here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lays the open notebook down beside the rim. The letters match.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: I could call this a coincidence, friend. I'd like to. It doesn't explain a thing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The word sinks. Its reflection stays on the surface one moment longer.

scene.memory: The word the word you offered appeared twice, once before you formed it.

scene.title: Who gets to know

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You write down what happened at the rim: the same word, already there before you offered it. You put the date beneath it.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: I'd like to fold that page away, friend. I can hear myself reaching for another comforting explanation.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: But you were there too. Do we tell the household what we saw, or keep the account between us while we look into it?

scene.memory: You decided who would hear the first account of the word that appeared twice.

options.label: Tell the household what we saw.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: You bring the account to the shared table. Those who read it add their initials beneath the date.

response.speaker: fox
response.text: I'll tell them what happened. I'll say I don't know why. You can stop me if I start making it sound safer than it is.

options.label: Keep the account between us for now.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: You fold the dated account and keep it with you. Ember leaves the outside blank.

response.speaker: fox
response.text: Between us, then. When you want someone else to read it, you can be the one to open it.
